title: Identity-composition squares in higher operation coordinates
statement: Fix a six-functor operation datum S [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and a finite-type space X. At each integral, rational and common-stage coefficient category A, let U be the recorded identity pullback, T:A×A→A the recorded uncurried tensor and μ the components of projectionPullbackTensor [lem-sf-common-projection-pullback-tensor-compatibility] for the proper identity square. Let c_M:U(M)≅U(U(M)) be the supplied pullback compositor for identity followed by identity, precomposed with its equality transport. Then μ_{M,L} followed by T(c_M,c_L) = c_{T(M,L)} followed by U(μ_{M,L}) followed by μ_{U(M),U(L)} for all M,L in A. These are raw composition squares: neither an identity unit e nor an identity-unit tensor equation occurs in their hypotheses or conclusion.

proof.text: Choose the strict coefficient-system realization from integralCompactificationSystemRealization. The coefficient convention makes l a unit in the base field and every residue field. Use the recorded whole-system tensor reduction isomorphism t and pullback comparison p. integralProperTensorPullbackReduction, after multiplying by p and tensoring its forward components, gives R(mu);t;W(p,p)=p;V(t);nu. integralDatumPullCompositionReduction gives R(c);p_U;V(p)=p;d, including the equality transport from identity composed with identity to identity.

For an arbitrary coefficient functor R with these two comparison equations, postcompose the images of the two proposed tensor-composition paths with t at the twice-pulled inputs and W(p_U,p_U);W(V(p),V(p)). Naturality of t,p,nu,d and functoriality identify the resulting paths with p;V(t) followed by the two system composition paths. Cancel the comparison isomorphisms. The system paths agree by integralSystemTensorComposition; reflect equality by faithfulness of whole-system integral reduction. No identity unit and no faithfulness of individual finite evaluations is used.

For rational coefficients apply the same categorical calculation in the forward direction to scalar localization. rationalProjectionPullTensorSquare gives the tensor comparison equation after the projection comparison is identified with the specified canonical map by its HEq normalization; rationalization.pullComposition supplies the compositor equation. Every rational object is the localization of its underlying integral object, so the integral square gives the rational square on all objects.

For a finite coefficient field F form the operation datum with higher operations coefficientStages F and its recorded coefficientIntegralNormalization. The rational conclusion just proved applies there. commonProjectionPullbackTensorCompatibility gives the inclusion tensor equation, while commonStageComparison F preserves pullComposition. Thus the same calculation proves the common square on included objects. Choose a field containing both input stages and use isoToStage on both inputs. Naturality of the two composite natural transformations transports that square to the original objects. Equality transports are retained throughout.

theorem higherTensor_identityComposition (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) :
    (∀ X : SixFunctorSpace D,
      letI : IsProper (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).hom.left := by
        change IsProper (𝟙 X.obj.left)
        infer_instance
      let U := S.higher.integral.pull (𝟙 X)
      let T := Functor.uncurry.obj (S.higher.integralTensor X)
      let μ := fun M L ↦
        ((projectionPullbackTensor (S.higher.integralExchange
          (compactSupportProperSquare (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X)))).hom.app M).app L
      let c : ∀ M, U.obj M ≅ U.obj (U.obj M) := fun M ↦
        eqToIso (congrArg (fun f ↦ (S.higher.integral.pull f).obj M)
          (Category.id_comp (𝟙 X)).symm) ≪≫
          (S.higher.integral.pullComposition (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X)).app M
      ∀ M L, μ M L ≫ T.map (Prod.mkHom (c M).hom (c L).hom) =
        (c (T.obj (M, L))).hom ≫ U.map (μ M L) ≫ μ (U.obj M) (U.obj L)) ∧
    (∀ X : SixFunctorSpace D,
      letI : IsProper (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).hom.left := by
        change IsProper (𝟙 X.obj.left)
        infer_instance
      let U := S.higher.rational.pull (𝟙 X)
      let T := Functor.uncurry.obj (S.higher.rationalTensor X)
      let μ := fun M L ↦
        ((projectionPullbackTensor (S.higher.rationalExchange
          (compactSupportProperSquare (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X)))).hom.app M).app L
      let c : ∀ M, U.obj M ≅ U.obj (U.obj M) := fun M ↦
        eqToIso (congrArg (fun f ↦ (S.higher.rational.pull f).obj M)
          (Category.id_comp (𝟙 X)).symm) ≪≫
          (S.higher.rational.pullComposition (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X)).app M
      ∀ M L, μ M L ≫ T.map (Prod.mkHom (c M).hom (c L).hom) =
        (c (T.obj (M, L))).hom ≫ U.map (μ M L) ≫ μ (U.obj M) (U.obj L)) ∧
    (∀ X : SixFunctorSpace D,
      letI : IsProper (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).hom.left := by
        change IsProper (𝟙 X.obj.left)
        infer_instance
      let U := S.closure.commonStage.pull (𝟙 X)
      let T := Functor.uncurry.obj (S.closure.commonStageTensor X)
      let μ := fun M L ↦
        ((projectionPullbackTensor (S.closure.commonStageExchange
          (compactSupportProperSquare (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X)))).hom.app M).app L
      let c : ∀ M, U.obj M ≅ U.obj (U.obj M) := fun M ↦
        eqToIso (congrArg (fun f ↦ (S.closure.commonStage.pull f).obj M)
          (Category.id_comp (𝟙 X)).symm) ≪≫
          (S.closure.commonStage.pullComposition (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X)).app M
      ∀ M L, μ M L ≫ T.map (Prod.mkHom (c M).hom (c L).hom) =
        (c (T.obj (M, L))).hom ≫ U.map (μ M L) ≫ μ (U.obj M) (U.obj L))
